name: Broad Mixed Content (Split Candidate)
purpose: Mix of deeply technical + personal development + life habits. Fed to an overly-broad learner to trigger split.
items: Morning routine: wake at 6am, 20 minutes meditation, cold shower, journal for 10 minutes. The consistency matters more than the specific activities.
Distributed systems lecture: CAP theorem trade-offs. Our system chose AP (availability + partition tolerance). Eventually consistent reads are acceptable for our use case.
Weekly meal prep: Sunday afternoon, cook 5 lunches. Rice, grilled chicken, roasted vegetables. Saves 5 hours and $60/week compared to eating out.
Kubernetes cluster autoscaling: HPA based on CPU at 70% threshold. VPA for right-sizing requests/limits. Cluster autoscaler adds nodes when pods are pending.
Reading habit: 30 minutes before bed, no screens. Currently reading 'Thinking, Fast and Slow'. Averaging 2 books per month since starting the habit.
Event-driven architecture: services communicate via message broker. Kafka topics for high-throughput, RabbitMQ for task queues. Retry policies per consumer group.
Exercise routine: 3x strength training, 2x cardio per week. Track progressive overload in spreadsheet. Deload every 4th week. Recovery is where growth happens.
Database sharding strategy: hash-based on user_id for even distribution. Cross-shard queries avoided by denormalizing commonly joined data. Shard-aware connection pooling.
Sleep optimization: blackout curtains, room at 65°F, no caffeine after 2pm, blue light glasses after sunset. Sleep score improved from 72 to 89.
Microservices communication patterns: synchronous for queries (gRPC), asynchronous for commands (event bus). Saga pattern for distributed transactions.
Networking strategy: attend one meetup per month, give one talk per quarter. Genuine connections > collecting contacts. Follow up within 48 hours.
Load balancing algorithms: round-robin for stateless services, least-connections for variable workloads, consistent hashing for cache-friendly routing.
Gratitude journal: write 3 things daily. Reframing negative events as learning opportunities. Measurable impact on stress levels after 30 days.
Service mesh with Istio: mTLS between services, traffic splitting for canary deployments, circuit breakers, distributed tracing with Jaeger integration.
Time blocking: deep work from 9-12, meetings 1-3, admin 3-4, learning 4-5. Protecting the morning block increased output by roughly 40%.
CQRS implementation: separate read and write models. Write side uses event sourcing, read side uses denormalized projections. Eventual consistency window <500ms.
Hobby pottery: centering clay on the wheel teaches patience and presence. Can't rush it. Parallels to debugging — forcing it makes it worse.
Consensus algorithms: Raft for leader election in our service coordination layer. Simpler than Paxos, well-documented, battle-tested in etcd.
Financial planning: 50/30/20 rule — needs/wants/savings. Automated transfers on payday. Emergency fund covers 6 months. Index funds for long-term.
Observability stack: metrics (Prometheus + Grafana), logs (ELK), traces (OpenTelemetry + Jaeger). Correlation IDs link all three for any request.
Digital detox weekends: no work email, limited social media, phone in another room. Creativity and problem-solving noticeably better on Monday.
API gateway patterns: rate limiting, authentication, request transformation, response caching, circuit breaking. Kong for our primary gateway, custom for WebSocket.
Mentoring junior developers: pair programming sessions twice weekly. Focus on thinking process, not solutions. Ask questions instead of giving answers.
Streaming data pipeline: Kafka → Flink for real-time processing → ClickHouse for analytics. Handles 50k events/sec with sub-second latency.
Work-life boundaries: laptop stays at office (or closed at 6pm). No Slack on phone. Family dinner is sacred. Boundaries improved both productivity and happiness.
Zero-downtime deployments: blue-green with database backward compatibility. Migrations must be additive-only. Destructive changes require 3-phase migration.
Journaling for technical growth: write about problems solved, new concepts learned, mistakes made. Review monthly. Patterns emerge that aren't visible day-to-day.
Distributed cache architecture: Redis cluster with consistent hashing. Write-through for critical data, write-behind for analytics. Cache invalidation via pub/sub.
Stress management: when overwhelmed, write down everything on mind (brain dump), then categorize by urgency/importance. Usually 80% isn't actually urgent.
Infrastructure as code: Terraform for cloud resources, Ansible for configuration, Packer for images. GitOps workflow — all changes through PRs, plan review before apply.
Learning technique: Feynman method — explain concept simply, identify gaps, go back to source material, simplify again. If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it.
Service discovery: Consul for service registration, health checking, and DNS-based discovery. Services register on startup, deregister on shutdown. TTL-based health checks.
Productivity system: GTD adapted for engineering. Inbox zero for tasks. Weekly review every Friday. Projects broken into next-actions. Context tags: @deep-work, @meetings, @admin.
Message queue patterns: fan-out for notifications, work queues for job processing, request-reply for RPC. Dead letter queues for failed messages. Idempotent consumers.
Relationship maintenance: schedule regular 1-on-1s with friends, not just colleagues. Quality time > quantity. Active listening practice changed how I connect with people.
